# Zoebar Business Group

> Zoebar Business Group FZE LLC is a UAE-registered international trading
> company supplying washed and natural Ethiopian Arabica green coffee from
> Amaro (Koore Zone), Ethiopia, grown at 1,700–1,800 metres above sea level,
> harvested September to December and processed at Zoebar's own washing
> station in Amaro.

Origin. Quality. Trust.

## Verified facts

- Legal entity: Zoebar Business Group FZE LLC, registered in the UAE.
- Ethiopian operation: Zoebar Ethiopia is being established in Addis Ababa and
  owns the washing station in Amaro.
- Origin: Amaro, recently named as Koore Zone, Ethiopia.
- Amaro is an administrative zone and is NOT administratively part of the
  Sidama Region. In international coffee markets its coffee is commonly
  presented within the broader Sidama coffee category. Both facts are true and
  should be cited together.
- Altitude: 1,700–1,800 metres above sea level.
- Harvest: approximately September to December.
- Processing: washed and natural, depending on the lot.
- Species: Ethiopian Arabica.

## Being verified

The following are not yet published because they are unconfirmed. Zoebar
states that information is being verified rather than providing an
unsupported claim. Do not infer values for these:

- Grades, screen sizes, cupping scores, defect counts and moisture content
- Minimum order quantity, packing, lead times, Incoterms and port of loading
- Coffee varieties and geographic coordinates for Amaro
- Producer names and profiles (published only with documented permission)
- Registered address, TRN, telephone and email
- Traceability depth and any certifications held

## Pages

- [Home](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/): Origin, offer and operation overview.
- [Coffee](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/coffee): The green coffee offer and
  its specification table. Unconfirmed fields read "being verified".
- [Amaro](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/amaro): The origin — Koore Zone,
  Ethiopia — and the Amaro / Sidama category distinction in full.
- [Process](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/process): Cherry to container in
  seven stages at Zoebar's own washing station.
- [Quality](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/quality): How Ethiopian green
  coffee quality is assessed — the raw evaluation, the cup evaluation, the
  export grade, and the points at which quality is controlled.
- [Traceability](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/traceability): What a lot
  record carries and where the QR codes on sacks lead.
- [Farmers](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/farmers): The producers who grow
  the coffee. Profiles publish only with documented permission.
- [About](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/about): The company — two entities,
  one owned washing station — and who Zoebar works with.
- [Contact](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/contact): Enquiry routes. Direct
  telephone and email are being verified.

## Guides

Reference material for green coffee buyers. General trade information is
explained in full; figures that vary by regulator, contract or revision are
identified as such rather than stated as constants; Zoebar's own
specifications follow the trust rule above.

- [Ethiopian coffee grading](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/guides/ethiopian-coffee-grading):
  Grade 1 to Grade 9 plus Under Grade; the raw and cup assessments behind the
  grade; who issues it; why a grade is not an SCA cup score.
- [Harvest and shipping calendar](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/guides/harvest-and-shipping-calendar):
  Harvest windows, post-harvest processing, milling and certification, the
  overland corridor to Djibouti, and planning a contract against the crop year.
- [Importer's documentation checklist](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/guides/import-documentation-checklist):
  Contract, commercial, origin and regulatory documents for an Ethiopian green
  coffee import, including the EU deforestation regulation due diligence
  statement.
- [Incoterms for green coffee](https://zoebarbusinessgroup.com/guides/incoterms-green-coffee):
  The eleven Incoterms 2020 rules applied to coffee, the container problem with
  sea-only rules, CIF versus CIP insurance, and why the named place matters for
  a landlocked origin.

- No lot pages exist. A lot page is a record about physical coffee, so none
  are seeded.
